name: Amber Enterprises India Ltd
about: Amber Enterprises India Ltd incorporated in 1956, has a 23.6% share in the total Room Air Conditioner market [1] and is a prominent solution provider for the Air conditioner OEM/ODM Industry in India. [2]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 32.1% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 22.2%.
EBITDA margin held roughly flat over 5 years (7.5% → 7.1%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 38% to 60% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 3.7%, 140 bps below a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹891 cr of profit, ₹2,478 cr of operating cash — conversion 2.78x.

context.speaker: Gupta
context.text: Whole Time Director, Mr. Sudhir Goyal - Group CFO, and Mr. Sanjay Arora, President of New Businesses. Let me first briefly talk about the strategic updates for the quarter. Firstly, in line with our continued efforts to strengthen and simplify the group structure, IL JIN had acquired the balance 40% stake in Power-One and 1.5% stake in Ascent Circuits through the issuance of CCPS, Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares, under a share swap arrangement. Consequently, both Power-One and Ascent Circuits are now wholly owned subsidiaries of IL JIN. Secondly, on the leadership front, I would like to acknowledge and thank Mr. Sanjay Arora for his immense contribution in shaping and value creation of our Electronics Division. As we enter the next phase of growth, he will take on the role of President, New Businesses and Group Evolution. Here, he will spearhead the Mobile Division and organizational development. We are confident that under his leadership, the mobile business will attain significant scale and emerge as a key player in the industry. We also welcome Mr. Satendra Singh as the CEO and Whole-Time Director of IL JIN Electronics. He is a seasoned industry professional with over three decades of experience in the electronic circuit sector, and prior to joining us, he served as the CEO of a listed EMS company and held other leadership positions with global organizations in his career. Coming to on the mobile business, after a thorough deliberation, we have decided to house mobile business under Amber, including production for OPPO, OnePlus, and Realme brands. Mobile business will operate under a dedicated and wholly owned subsidiary, namely Amber Digital Technologies. It is entering mobile-phone manufacturing for Oppo, OnePlus and Realme. Q1 FY27 revenue was INR3,888 crore; TTM revenue is INR13,606 crore.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore on 13% revenue growth, i.e. margins expanding (C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: In Q2 FY27 revenue rose 59.5% YoY but reported margin fell to 3.7% from 5.1% a year earlier, and PAT was down 106.2% YoY (a loss). The inputs contain no Q2 transcript explaining it.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Adjusted PAT of INR126 crore in Q1 FY27, INR141 crore before the purchase-price-allocation inventory charge (C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The adjustment excludes an INR123 crore exceptional loss and an INR15.35 crore PPA charge. TTM reported PAT is only INR90 crore on INR13,606 crore revenue (0.7%), and ROCE is 10%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Sidwal can grow about 40% in FY27 (G25, Q3 FY26).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: By Q1 FY27 the railway subsystem and defence division was guided at 30-35% growth and a 15-16% margin, after a quarter with pass-through sales and fixed-price tenders (G4, G5, C3). Consolidated FY27-to-date growth is 27.8%. Whether this is the same business, and whether the target was effectively trimmed, cannot be confirmed from the inputs.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Mobile manufacturing on schedule: trial Q4 FY27, commercial Q1 FY28, 8 million units in year 1 (G13, G1, G2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Dates are unchanged across two calls, but year-2 volume was raised from 13-15 million (G15) to 15-16 million (G3) before production began. No revenue or capex has been reported against it yet.

bull.point: Top-line momentum: Q2 FY27 revenue up 59.5% YoY, TTM revenue INR13,606 crore, 5-year revenue CAGR 32.1%.
Asset-light mobile option: three brands (Oppo, OnePlus, Realme), 8 million units in year 1 rising to 15-16 million in year 2, initial capex under INR50 crore, and dates held across two calls.
Underlying operating improvement in Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 28% against revenue up 13% (C2). 5-year CFO/PAT is 2.78, so cash generation exceeds reported profit.

bear.point: Profitability collapsed in Q2 FY27: margin 3.7% against 5.1% a year earlier, PAT down 106.2% YoY. TTM PAT is INR90 crore (0.7% of revenue) and ROCE is 10%.

Funding strain: borrowings INR4,723 crore, debt/equity 1.08 and 5-year FCF of minus INR880 crore, with about INR3,200 crore of Jewar capex and INR1,100-1,200 crore of FY27 capitalisation still to come.

Earnings quality: Q1 'adjusted' PAT strips out an INR123 crore exceptional loss and INR15.35 crore of PPA charges. Railway contracts are fixed-price against commodity, currency and a 35% wage shock. The cash-conversion cycle widened from 17 to 53 days in three years.

questions: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 59.5% but margin fell to 3.7% and PAT turned negative. How much of Q2 revenue was pass-through or trading supply (as in railway in Q1) or acquired businesses, and what was the organic operating margin?
Did Hosur trial production start in September 2026 as promised in Q3 FY26, and is mass production still due by January 2027? If not, what slipped?

With debt/equity at 1.08, 5-year FCF of minus INR880 crore and TTM PAT of INR90 crore, how will the INR3,200 crore Jewar capex be funded (debt, equity or subsidy), and what peak debt/equity do you plan for?
